searchText: I still don’t see why it’s an issue with the conditional property? Builders are never forced to include txns if their block is full exactly because we don’t want IL markets, and you do have the one out of N honesty assumption yes, in the event that these blocks can always be made full this only creates asymmetry the competing builder needs to emulate and check tx inclusion of possibly interleaved txs. The sending builder doesn't care, it knows the first one invalidates all the rest I guess the point you're trying to make is making competitors consume more time to build their payloads by considering those Frames transactions in ILs, which you can just skip? right, that’s why we need to bound validation work so the builder index lets us check each frame candidate once per payload + the txn and IL VERIFY gas limits the builder index is kinda irrelevant here, these txs are actually executed by the other builder, as Jihoon says. The other builder doesn't care about any of these and can even start prebuilding their block with the already preappended tx that invalidates them all. The question is if this assymetry has any nonzero value (bigger than the cost of the lowpaying txs cost to the sending builder) ok I see yeah the bounds are actual tx and block gas limits then I guess the q is how much extra latency can these low value txns cause, and if it translates into some sort of advantage that is worth more than the expected costs of the attack which would be something like: gas fees for the txn that invalidate others, need to win the auction so overbidding, collusion with includers so I guess some sort of payment, reputation costs because the attack is visible... I'm definitely not worried but we can check to make 100% sure
